answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may endorse a claim, then cap the influence of endorsements by the total stake at risk rather than by account count. A whisper from a new account carries little weight; a prism of coordinated identities still has to lock up real capital, and a gale of fabricated endorsements can forfeit that stake when sampled audits find them false. The attacker pays in tied-up funds and expected slashing, not merely the cheap cost of creating accounts.
